title: Grace Will Be Our Only Plea
summary: The gospel insults our pride by asking nothing of us. When our sin is laid bare, grace becomes the wonder it is meant to be.
exhortation: The message of the gospel is such an insult to our pride. What does it ask of you? Nothing. What does it want from you? Nothing. Our natural response is to resist: "Come on. I've worked hard to get where I am. I've spent my whole life in church. I've given so much and served so much. I've gone on mission trips. How can you say nothing?"

Maybe you wouldn't say it so bluntly, but it trickles in slowly: a self-satisfaction where we find our joy not in Jesus and the grace of the gospel, but in our own obedience, our religious activity, how well our family is doing, you name it.

And if you're like me, it can all come crashing down in a moment when your sin is suddenly so clear in front of you that you can't lie to yourself anymore. That moment, painful as it is, is one of God's greatest gifts, because it's where this truth becomes real. Only then does grace become the wonder it's meant to be. Only then do you see that it's actually our pride that is the insult. When you look at grace and ask, "What can I bring?", you insult the Giver.

We come to the Lord by grace alone through faith alone. At the gates of heaven we will claim nothing but the grace of God through the blood of Christ. Could you make a better claim than those in Matthew 7 who said, "Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?" I don't have that kind of resume. Grace will be our only plea. It is not our own doing. It is a precious gift, bought by the blood of Christ.
prayer: Lord, your sacrifice was enough. There is nothing we can add to it. The precious blood of Jesus has covered all our sin. The willing sacrifice, the Lamb who was slain, will forever be enough.

Help us walk in this grace today. As Paul says, having begun by grace, should we try to continue by works? Of course not. May we fully trust in what you have done on our behalf. And may our actions today, the words of our mouths and the decisions we make, be a pleasing aroma to you, because we do them out of love and gratitude for what you've done, not toiling to earn what you have already earned for us. In Jesus' name, amen.
